case_name: Joshinder Yadav v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

20 January 2014
Cr.A. No. 259 of 2009
The Judgment was delivered by : Ranjana Prakash Desai, J.
1. The appellant who was arraigned as Accused 2 was tried along with five other accused for offences punishable under Sections 498A and 302 read with Ss. 149 and 201 of the IPC by the 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Madhepura. The allegations against the accused, inter alia, were that they subjected one Bindula Devi to cruelty and harassment with a view to coercing her and her other relatives to meet their unlawful demand of property and that on her failure to fulfill their unlawful demand, in furtherance of their common object, they committed her murder and that they caused disappearance of her dead body with an intention to screen themselves from legal punishment.
2. Bindula Devi was married to Accused 1 Jaipraksh Yadav. The appellant and Accused 3 Shakun Devo Yadav are the brothers of Accused 1 Jaiprakash Yadav. Accused 4 Dani Dutta
facts: The appellant was tried along with five other accused for offences punishable under Sections 498A and 302 read with Ss. 149 and 201 of the IPC.
Bindula Devi was married to Accused 1 Jaiprakash Yadav.
Accused 2 is the brother of Accused 1 Jaiprakash Yadav, the husband of Bindula Devi.
The prosecution story is reflected in the evidence of Complainant PW-9 Debu Yadav, the father of Bindula Devi.
Bindula Devi was subjected to cruelty and harassment for dowry by the accused.
All the other witnesses, that is PW-2 to PW-7 turned hostile.
issues: Whether the appellant can be convicted under Section 498A of the IPC?
Whether the prosecution has established its case beyond reasonable doubt?
petitioner_arguments: The instant case rests on circumstantial evidence.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the appellant was party to any dowry demand or to any ill-treatment meted out to Bindula Devi.
Unless the circumstantial evidence is of required standard, conviction cannot be based on it.
respondent_arguments: The evidence on record establishes that all the accused were staying in houses situated in the same courtyard.
Evidence of PW-9 Debu Yadav and PW-10 Sachindra Yadav establishes the prosecution case.
Pertinently, the accused did not lodge any complaint to the police.
The fact that they left the house with all their belongings suggests their complicity.
court_reasoning: We have already referred to the evidence of father of Bindula Devi PW-9 Debu Yadav.
He has given a graphic account of the harassment and ill-treatment meted out to the deceased by the accused.
Implicit reliance can be placed on them.
Though, PW-10 Sachindra Yadav stated that Accused 1 Jaiprakash Yadav had separated from his brothers after marriage, he has clarified that all the brothers have their houses in a common courtyard.
holding: The conviction and sentence of the appellant under Section 498A of the IPC is therefore perfectly justified.
We reject the submission that the appellant did not join the other accused in treating Bindula Devi with cruelty.
